newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-SRI LANKA SEEK TO PROFIT FROM PAKISTAN INJURIES.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SRI LANKA SEEK TO PROFIT FROM PAKISTAN INJURIES.

text.p: Pakistan will be forced to cope without their twin spearheads Wasim Akram amd Waqar Younis when they take on Sri Lanka in the first test in Colombo on Saturday.
Akram is nursing an injured bowling arm, a result of excessive cricket, and Waqar has a fractured toe which has ruled him out of the tour.
It means that Pakistan's new-ball attack will consist of the inexperienced Mohammad Zahid and Shahid Nazir, who between them have played only five tests and captured 24 wickets.

Pakistan have already called for another fast bowler Mohammad Akram as Waqar's replacement, but at least have the knowledge that Zahid and Nazir were responsible for bowling their country to an innings and 13 runs win over New Zealand at Rawalpindi last November.
Zahid, making his test debut, captured 11 wickets in the match, including 7 for 66 in the second innings.

"It is a indeed a terrible blow for us without Wasim or Waqar, but we will have to carry on with it," said Pakistan coach Mushtaq Mohammad, aware his first-choice pair have claimed 538 test wickets between them.

Pakistan have also arrived in Sri Lanka for their short series of two tests without opening batsmen Saeed Anwar and Aamir Sohail. Anwar is suffering from a recurring stomach ailment, while Sohail was handed a two-year disciplinary ban by the Pakistan Cricket Board this week.
Rameez Raja will replace Akram as captain in the first test.
Against such a makeshift side, Sri Lanka will be looking to redeem themselves by winning the first test after their comprehensive defeat at the hands of New Zealand last month.
But Sri Lanka might be without opener Roshan Mahanama, who is recovering from a chipped left toe.
"We will leave our options open till the morning of the match to give Mahanama maximum opportunity to recover from the injury," said Bruce Yardley, Sri Lanka's coach.
In the event of Mahanama failing a fitness test, his place will go to 23-year-old newcomer Russell Arnold.

Sri Lanka (from): Arjuna Ranatunga (captain), Roshan Mahanama, Sanath Jayasuriya, Marvan Atapattu, Aravinda de Silva, Hashan Tillekeratne, Romesh Kaluwitharana, Chaminda Vaas, Muthiah Muralitharan, Kumara Dharmasena, Nuwan Zoysa, Sajeeva de Silva, Russell Arnold, Jayantha Silva, Sanjeeva Ranatunga.
Pakistan (from) : Rameez Raja (captain), Salim Elahi, Asif Mujtaba, Salim Malik, Inzamam-ul-Haq, Mohammad Wasim, Moin Khan, Saqlain Mushtaq, Shahid Nazir, Mohammad Zahid, Mushtaq Ahmed, Ijaz Ahmed.
Umpires: David Shepherd (England), Udaya Wickremasinghe (Sri Lanka).
